title: SEC: bt5.7 Sieve compile error DoS via admin script upload
description: In smtp/session.rs sieve_for_user(), a permanently-broken Sieve script (one that fails usenet_ipfs_sieve::compile()) causes every incoming message for that user to hit the DB, call compile(), fail, and return Err — issuing a 451 deferral to the sending MTA. The compile error is NOT cached (the cache only stores successfully-compiled scripts), so the compile attempt is repeated on every message delivery. An operator with Sieve admin API access can upload a broken script and cause permanent mail deferral for a target user. Trust level: operator-level (requires Sieve admin API access). Worst case: sustained mail deferral (no data loss — sending MTAs will retry). Impact: availability only, no confidentiality or integrity breach. Mitigation options: (1) cache the compile-error result and return 451 without re-compiling until the admin invalidates the entry, (2) validate script at upload time and reject broken scripts before storage (already done in put_script — so the only way to get a broken script in the DB is if the sieve interpreter version changes after upload). Note: validation at upload time (put_script returns 422 on parse error) is the primary defense; this is defense-in-depth concern.
